title: Unstrained C–C cleavage at a chosen bond
open: Can a chemist cleave a single, preselected C–C bond in an unstrained, multifunctional molecule and install new functionality in its place — without invoking ring-strain release, privileged directing groups, or destructive fragmentation elsewhere in the skeleton?
status: A longstanding skeletal-editing challenge. Alkyne-bridged palladium chemistry in 2025 enabled cleavage in unstrained ketones, esters and amides (Ding et al. (2025), *Modular esterification of unstrained carbonyls through palladium-catalyzed alkyne bridging C-C bond activation*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-64279-0](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-64279-0)); arbitrary backbone bonds remain substantially less accessible.
solved_when: A general experimental method exists that cleaves a chosen unstrained C–C bond and replaces it in multifunctional substrates, with no reliance on ring-strain release, directing groups, or collateral fragmentation.
why: It would let molecular frameworks be diversified after their construction, rather than rebuilt from scratch for each desired variant.
key_works: Ding et al. (2025), *Modular esterification of unstrained carbonyls through palladium-catalyzed alkyne bridging C-C bond activation*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-64279-0](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-64279-0).

title: Independent selection of aromatic rings for saturation
open: Hydrogenate a chosen ring in a molecule containing several electronically similar arenes, with independent control of ring selection and stereochemistry while retaining other reducible groups.
status: Longstanding. Directed ruthenium saturation reported in 2025 by Yu, Yiu, Zhang and Dong (2025), *Site-selective Ru-catalysed saturation of unactivated arenes via directed 6π activation*, [DOI:10.1038/s41929-025-01404-8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41929-025-01404-8), selects the arene adjacent to a directing moiety, including complex substrates and gram-scale examples; freely selecting other rings remains open.
solved_when: A method exists that selects which aromatic ring is saturated by design rather than by a directing group's position, with stereochemical control, and tolerates other reducible groups intact, demonstrated on complex substrates including gram-scale examples.
why: Provides three-dimensional drug analogues without rebuilding the molecule.
key_works: Yu, Yiu, Zhang and Dong (2025), *Site-selective Ru-catalysed saturation of unactivated arenes via directed 6π activation*, [DOI:10.1038/s41929-025-01404-8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41929-025-01404-8).

title: Position-programmable carbon-to-nitrogen ring editing
open: Can we replace a chosen ring carbon with nitrogen in a densely substituted arene or heteroarene while leaving the rest of the substitution pattern intact — and do so at a position we select freely among competing candidates using practical reagents?
status: The area has developed rapidly since the early 2020s. In 2025, Puriņins, Nakahara and Levin demonstrated a pyridine-to-pyridazine conversion via azide introduction and photochemical rearrangement (*Bridging the pyridine-pyridazine synthesis gap by skeletal editing*, DOI:10.1126/science.adx4762); general positional editing remains open.
solved_when: A general method exists for position-programmable carbon-to-nitrogen skeletal editing of densely substituted arenes and heteroarenes, in which the replacement position is independently selectable at competing sites with practical reagents and the remaining substitution pattern is preserved.
why: It would let medicinal chemists change a ring scaffold late in a synthesis, unlocking scaffold hopping without redoing entire synthetic routes.
key_works: Puriņš, Nakahara and Levin (2025), *Bridging the pyridine-pyridazine synthesis gap by skeletal editing*, [DOI:10.1126/science.adx4762](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adx4762).

title: Carbon isotope exchange at arbitrary skeletal positions
open: Can a chosen skeletal carbon in an intact complex molecule be swapped for an isotope-labeled carbon — without rebuilding the skeleton, erasing stereochemical information, or extensively scrambling the label? Formally, the goal is a general method for position-selective carbon isotope exchange that preserves molecular architecture across arbitrary skeletal sites.
status: Direct exchange has advanced for selected functional groups: vanadium-mediated exchange of terminal alkenes was demonstrated in 2025 (Krivovicheva et al. (2025), *Vanadium-Mediated Carbon Isotope Exchange of Terminal Alkenes*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.5c05880](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c05880)). Buried saturated carbons and arbitrary position selection remain open.
solved_when: A general exchange method exists that (i) reaches an arbitrary chosen skeletal position, including buried saturated carbons, and (ii) operates on an intact complex molecule without skeleton reconstruction, loss of stereochemical information, or extensive label scrambling.
why: It would simplify the preparation of tracers and enable quantitative studies of molecular fate, e.g. rapid site-specific radiotracer synthesis for medical imaging and identifiable metabolic-flux models in systems biology.
key_works: Krivovicheva et al. (2025), *Vanadium-Mediated Carbon Isotope Exchange of Terminal Alkenes*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.5c05880](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c05880).

title: Addressable epimerization of every sugar stereocenter
open: Can any single stereocenter of an unprotected sugar — or of a chosen residue within an oligosaccharide — be inverted at will, leaving every other stereocenter and all glycosidic linkages untouched? More formally, the goal is a general method for addressable epimerization of each position in complex glycans.
status: Selective rare-sugar epimerizations were demonstrated by Wang, Carder and Wendlandt (2020), *Synthesis of rare sugar isomers through site-selective epimerization* ([DOI:10.1038/s41586-020-1937-1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-1937-1)). Kinetic-network control reported in 2026 extended selected transformations, including GlcNAc-to-GalNAc. Independent access to every position in complex glycans remains unresolved.
solved_when: A demonstrated method can invert each stereocenter of an unprotected sugar or a selected oligosaccharide residue, independently and selectively, while preserving all other centers and glycosidic linkages.
why: It would convert abundant sugars into otherwise costly stereochemical building blocks, unlocking cheap access to rare-sugar isomers for synthesis and medicine.
key_works: Wang, Carder and Wendlandt (2020), *Synthesis of rare sugar isomers through site-selective epimerization*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-020-1937-1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-1937-1).

title: Stereodivergent synthesis of distant acyclic stereocenters
open: Can one starting-material set be turned into every possible configuration of several independently positioned, nonadjacent stereocenters in an acyclic chain, without redesigning the route for each isomer?
status: A multidecade objective; nickel chain-walking chemistry reported online in 2025 (Ju et al., 2025/2026, *Stereodivergent construction of non-adjacent stereocentres via migratory functionalization of alkenes*, [DOI:10.1038/s41557-025-01994-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-025-01994-7)) accesses all four stereoisomers for selected 1,3- and 1,4-related centers, while longer distances and more centers remain open.
solved_when: A single synthetic strategy, from a common set of starting materials, delivers all stereoisomeric combinations of three or more nonadjacent acyclic stereocenters at separations beyond the 1,3- and 1,4-related cases already demonstrated, with route redesign avoided for each isomer.
why: It would let drug-discovery teams separate pure stereochemical effects from scaffold effects, since all stereoisomers of a candidate become accessible on demand.
key_works: Ju et al. (2025/2026), *Stereodivergent construction of non-adjacent stereocentres via migratory functionalization of alkenes*, [DOI:10.1038/s41557-025-01994-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-025-01994-7).

title: General mild catalytic amidation without coupling reagents
open: Can amides be formed from unactivated carboxylic acids and amines using only a catalyst — no stoichiometric coupling reagent — under mild, concentrated conditions? The target is a single catalytic platform that handles diverse substrates, including sterically hindered and unprotected ones, with negligible racemization.
status: The problem is decades old. Phosphorus/catechol catalysis reported in 2025 by Nagano et al. (*Study on Phosphorus Compound/Catechol-Catalyzed Dehydrative Amidation and Its Database Development for Machine Learning*, [DOI:10.1002/chem.202500955](https://doi.org/10.1002/chem.202500955)) adds a direct-amidation platform, but jointly achieving broad scope, water tolerance, low temperature, and catalyst recovery remains open.
solved_when: A catalytic direct-amidation method is demonstrated that works across diverse unactivated acids and amines, including hindered and unprotected substrates, operates under mild, concentrated conditions, gives negligible racemization, uses no stoichiometric activator, and tolerates water while permitting catalyst recovery.
why: It would remove the major reagent and purification burdens that stoichiometric coupling reagents impose on pharmaceutical synthesis.
key_works: Nagano et al. (2025), *Study on Phosphorus Compound/Catechol-Catalyzed Dehydrative Amidation and Its Database Development for Machine Learning*, [DOI:10.1002/chem.202500955](https://doi.org/10.1002/chem.202500955).

title: Main-group carbonylation with complete catalytic turnover
open: Can a main-group element — not a transition metal — serve as the catalyst in a carbonylation cycle that runs to completion and restarts? Formally, this means a cycle in which CO is repeatedly inserted, the resulting acyl group is selectively transferred to a substrate, and the main-group catalyst is regenerated in each turnover, with no stoichiometric consumption of the metal.
status: Reversible main-group CO insertion and extrusion remain sparsely developed. Bismuth compounds enabled reversible visible-light-driven steps in 2025 (Geist et al., *Diaryl Bismuthides and Acyl Bismuthanes Enable Visible-Light-Induced Reversible Carbon Monoxide Insertion and Extrusion*, DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-66412-5); broadly useful complete synthesis cycles remain open.
solved_when: A demonstrated main-group carbonylation cycle is achieved in which CO insertion, selective acyl-group transfer, and catalyst regeneration all proceed repeatedly over multiple turnovers without stoichiometric metal consumption.
why: It would deliver new, transition-metal-free catalyst architectures for making carbonyl-containing chemicals.
key_works: Geist et al. (2025), *Diaryl Bismuthides and Acyl Bismuthanes Enable Visible-Light-Induced Reversible Carbon Monoxide Insertion and Extrusion*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-66412-5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-66412-5).

title: Broad photochemical deracemization without molecular damage
open: Can a single photochemical strategy convert an arbitrary racemate into either chosen enantiomer on demand, across diverse stereogenic motifs, while leaving other stereocenters and photolabile groups intact? More formally, the goal is deracemization with efficient photon use at practical temperatures.
status: The field has been rapidly expanding since the 2010s. Copper-catalyzed photoderacemization reported in 2025 (Zhong et al., DOI:10.1038/s41586-025-08784-8) covered secondary and tertiary alkyl halides, including tetrasubstituted centers; general transferability to other motifs remains open.
solved_when: A method exists that converts racemates to either enantiomer across diverse stereogenic motifs while preserving other stereocenters and photolabile groups, with efficient photon use and practical temperatures.
why: It converts an entire racemate into a selected enantiomer, avoiding the yield limitation inherent to simple resolution.
key_works: Zhong et al. (2025), *Photoinduced copper-catalysed deracemization of alkyl halides*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-025-08784-8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-08784-8).

title: Efficient chemical motors under sustained useful loads
open: Can we build a fully synthetic, chemically fueled molecular motor that does sustained useful work against external loads, with a fuel-to-work efficiency, reliability, and speed that can actually be quantified and controlled?
status: Synthetic molecular motors have been developed for decades, and catalysis-driven polymer-gel contraction was demonstrated in 2025 (Wang et al. (2025), *Transducing chemical energy through catalysis by an artificial molecular motor*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-024-08288-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08288-x)); efficient reusable operation under diverse prescribed loads remains open.
solved_when: A synthetic chemical motor operates reusably under diverse prescribed external loads, delivering sustained work with quantified fuel-to-work efficiency, reliability, and controllable speed.
why: It converts molecular-scale motion into practical actuation and transport, the step needed for molecular machines to do real work rather than merely move.
key_works: Wang et al. (2025), *Transducing chemical energy through catalysis by an artificial molecular motor*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-024-08288-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08288-x).

title: Independent sequence and stereochemical programming of polymers
open: Can the stereochemical configuration at each stereogenic center along a polymer chain be programmed independently of the chain's already-specified monomer sequence — going beyond repeating motifs and stereoregular blocks to arbitrary joint control? Formally: given a prescribed long-chain connectivity sequence together with a target assignment of configurations at each stereogenic unit, can synthesis realize both simultaneously?
status: Longstanding problem. A 2025 ring-opening polymerization platform (Wang et al. (2025), *High-performance recyclable polymers enabled by stereo- and sequence-controlled polymerization*, [DOI:10.1038/s41557-025-01828-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-025-01828-6)) controlled stereochemistry and sequence sufficiently to produce selected AB and ABA materials; arbitrary joint programming remains open.
solved_when: A synthetic method demonstrates independent assignment of stereogenic configurations along an already prescribed long-chain sequence, beyond repeating motifs or stereoregular blocks — i.e., arbitrary combinations of sequence and stereochemistry are accessible in a single polymer.
why: It would decouple composition, monomer ordering, and chirality as design variables, letting each be tuned independently to map and optimize material properties.
key_works: Wang et al. (2025), *High-performance recyclable polymers enabled by stereo- and sequence-controlled polymerization*, [DOI:10.1038/s41557-025-01828-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-025-01828-6).

title: Universal tacticity control in radical polymerization
open: Can stereoregularity (tacticity) be directly controlled in radical polymerization across a broad range of vinyl monomers — including those with strongly polar substituents — without resorting to special bulky pendant groups that must later be replaced? Formally, the goal is a general method achieving high tacticity control that does not depend on transformable pendant-group chemistry.
status: A longstanding gap. Pan and Ouchi (2025) obtained approximately 99% meso-dyad polyacrylamides using a transformable bulky pendant in *Post-polymerization modification enabling library synthesis of highly isotactic polyacrylamides carrying different pendant groups* ([DOI:10.1038/s42004-025-01663-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42004-025-01663-3)); general direct control remains open.
solved_when: A radical polymerization method demonstrates tacticity control across diverse vinyl monomers, including strongly polar ones, by direct means — that is, without requiring special bulky pendant groups followed by their replacement, and reaching meso-dyad content comparable to the ~99% achieved with the indirect approach.
why: It would unite the practical advantages of radical processing (tolerance of polar functionality, mild conditions, scale) with precision control over thermal and mechanical properties, which currently are only accessible via indirect, monomer-specific workarounds.
key_works: Pan and Ouchi (2025), *Post-polymerization modification enabling library synthesis of highly isotactic polyacrylamides carrying different pendant groups*, [DOI:10.1038/s42004-025-01663-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42004-025-01663-3).

title: Polypropylene-to-propylene without large coproduct streams
open: Can real polypropylene waste be converted selectively back into propylene? Formally, the goal is to depolymerize actual polypropylene waste into propylene at high carbon yield, without generating large unwanted coproduct streams, requiring excessive reagent co-feed, or suffering rapid catalyst deactivation.
status: Longstanding problem. Base-metal ethenolysis reported in 2024 converted polypropylene and mixed polyolefins to light olefins, including propylene/isobutylene mixtures (Conk et al. (2024), *Polyolefin waste to light olefins with ethylene and base-metal heterogeneous catalysts*, [DOI:10.1126/science.adq7316](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adq7316)); propylene-focused circularity remains open.
solved_when: A process converts real (not idealized) polypropylene waste to propylene at high carbon yield while avoiding large coproduct streams, excessive reagent co-feed, and rapid deactivation; no further quantitative targets are specified in the record.
why: Recovering propylene closes the loop on polypropylene, returning the original high-volume monomer from post-consumer products rather than downcycling it.
key_works: Conk et al. (2024), *Polyolefin waste to light olefins with ethylene and base-metal heterogeneous catalysts*, [DOI:10.1126/science.adq7316](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adq7316).

title: Closed-reagent-loop silicone recycling
open: Can the diverse streams of filled and cross-linked silicone waste be recycled through a process that regenerates its own reagents rather than consuming them — recovering chlorosilane feedstocks while keeping catalyst loss and impurity accumulation controlled over long operation?
status: Gallium/BCl₃ chemistry reported in 2025 (Vu et al., *Gallium-catalyzed recycling of silicone waste with boron trichloride to yield key chlorosilanes*, DOI:10.1126/science.adv0919) converted varied silicone wastes into key chlorosilanes near quantitatively at 40 °C; closing auxiliary reagent loops and demonstrating prolonged plant operation remain open.
solved_when: A process recycles varied filled and cross-linked silicone wastes, recovers both silicone feedstocks (e.g., key chlorosilanes at near-quantitative yield, as achieved at 40 °C) and the auxiliary reagents in closed loop, and demonstrates prolonged plant operation with catalyst loss and impurity accumulation controlled.
why: It conserves the embedded silicon-processing energy and valuable feedstocks locked in silicone waste, which currently cannot be recovered from filled and cross-linked materials.
key_works: Vu et al. (2025), *Gallium-catalyzed recycling of silicone waste with boron trichloride to yield key chlorosilanes*, [DOI:10.1126/science.adv0919](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adv0919).

title: Reactive oxidant in particulate methane monooxygenase
open: What is the oxygen-derived species that actually cleaves methane's C–H bond in active, membrane-bound particulate methane monooxygenase, and how fast is it formed and decayed? A complete answer identifies the oxidant structurally and establishes its formation and decay kinetics under turnover conditions.
status: Structural studies have narrowed copper-site assignments. Calculations in 2024–2025 proposed distinguishable oxidant-generation mechanisms — including the proposal of Lundgren et al. (2025), *The CuB site in particulate methane monooxygenase may be used to produce hydrogen peroxide* [DOI:10.1039/D4DT03301A] — but these await decisive turnover experiments.
solved_when: The reactive oxidant in active pMMO is identified, and its formation and decay kinetics are experimentally established; decisive turnover experiments distinguish among the proposed oxidant-generation mechanisms.
why: Knowing the oxidant and its kinetics supplies mechanistic guidance for selective methane oxidation, with applications including fugitive-methane mitigation.
key_works: Lundgren et al. (2025), *The CuB site in particulate methane monooxygenase may be used to produce hydrogen peroxide*, [DOI:10.1039/D4DT03301A](https://doi.org/10.1039/D4DT03301A).

title: Coordinated protocell genome and membrane reproduction
open: Can a chemically simple protocell sustain coordinated reproduction — genome copying together with membrane growth, division, and inheritance of the genetic material — across many generations without any protein machinery?
status: Individual components have been demonstrated for decades; mixed-sequence RNA copying inside fatty-acid vesicles was shown in 2018 (O’Flaherty et al., *Copying of Mixed-Sequence RNA Templates inside Model Protocells*, DOI:10.1021/jacs.8b00639), but fully integrated hereditary reproduction remains open.
solved_when: A constructed compartment system demonstrates that genome replication and membrane division remain coupled and heritable over successive generations, with no protein enzymes involved.
why: It would establish a concrete, buildable intermediate step between pure chemistry and living cells, showing that coordinated self-reproduction does not require evolved protein machinery.
key_works: O’Flaherty et al. (2018), *Copying of Mixed-Sequence RNA Templates inside Model Protocells*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.8b00639](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.8b00639).

title: Protocell nutrient entry without genome leakage
open: Can we build a protocell membrane that lets replication feedstocks in while keeping genetic polymers from leaking out, and stays stable under the ionic conditions and environmental cycles that RNA copying requires?
status: The permeability–retention conflict is longstanding. Vesicle experiments in 2018 (O’Flaherty et al., *Copying of Mixed-Sequence RNA Templates inside Model Protocells*, DOI:10.1021/jacs.8b00639) admitted short oligonucleotides; compatibility across repeated reproduction cycles remains unresolved.
solved_when: A membrane is demonstrated that admits replication feedstocks, retains genetic polymers, and remains stable under the ions and repeated environmental cycles required by copying.
why: Without such a membrane, replicating compartments either starve for lack of feedstocks or lose their hereditary information through leakage.
key_works: O’Flaherty et al. (2018), *Copying of Mixed-Sequence RNA Templates inside Model Protocells*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.8b00639](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.8b00639).

title: Self-replenishing prebiotic nucleotide activation
open: Can a prebiotic chemical network keep nucleotides activated — and re-activate them as they are consumed — using only plausible environmental energy sources, while remaining compatible with template-directed copying? A satisfactory answer must explicitly track and deal with inhibitory by-products rather than assuming them away.
status: The underlying activation chemistry is decades old. Photochemical activation with recycling was demonstrated in 2018 (Mariani et al. (2018), *A Light-Releasable Potentially Prebiotic Nucleotide Activating Agent*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.8b05189](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.8b05189)); integrating such activation into sustained genome replication remains open.
solved_when: A copying-compatible network is demonstrated in which nucleotide activation is sustained (i.e., activator is replenished or regenerated continuously, not supplied once) by plausible environmental energy, with a quantitative accounting of inhibitory by-products and demonstration that they do not shut down copying.
why: Copying chemistry consumes chemical free energy; without a self-replenishing activation source, any model of sustained genome replication is quietly living off a finite stock of activated fuel.
key_works: Mariani et al. (2018), *A Light-Releasable Potentially Prebiotic Nucleotide Activating Agent*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.8b05189](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.8b05189).

title: Parasite-resistant prebiotic replicator communities
open: Can a chemically simple replicator population survive alongside faster parasitic sequences while still preserving innovation and cooperation under plausible prebiotic compartment cycles?
status: Transient compartmentalization suppressed parasite takeover experimentally in Matsumura et al. (2016), *Transient compartmentalization of RNA replicators prevents extinction due to parasites* ([PubMed record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27940874/)); however, comparable robustness with wholly prebiotic replication chemistry remains open.
solved_when: A replicator community is demonstrated, experimentally and/or theoretically, that resists parasitic takeover while maintaining cooperative innovation under compartment cycling conditions compatible with prebiotic chemistry.
why: It addresses the evolutionary failure mode — parasite-driven extinction — that lies beyond merely achieving successful replication, and thus tests whether Darwinian evolution can genuinely take hold prebiotically.
key_works: Matsumura et al. (2016), *Transient compartmentalization of RNA replicators prevents extinction due to parasites*, [PubMed record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27940874/).

title: Why D-RNA became coupled to L-proteins
open: Why did life couple right-handed (D) sugars in RNA to left-handed (L) amino acids in proteins? We seek mechanisms — whether historical contingency or an underlying chemical bias — that can be identified and experimentally discriminated as the source of this specific chiral pairing.
status: A longstanding specificity question. Tests of 15 self-aminoacylating ribozymes in 2024 (Kenchel et al. (2024), *Prebiotic chiral transfer from self-aminoacylating ribozymes may favor either handedness*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-024-52362-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-52362-x)) found both chiral preferences, challenging a universal D-RNA-to-L-amino-acid bias.
solved_when: A mechanism (or set of mechanisms) establishing the D-RNA/L-amino-acid relationship is identified and experimentally discriminated from alternatives, including a determination of whether the pairing reflects contingency or chemical bias.
why: It explains why biology adopted this particular handedness pairing, a question distinct from explaining homochirality itself.
key_works: Kenchel et al. (2024), *Prebiotic chiral transfer from self-aminoacylating ribozymes may favor either handedness*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-024-52362-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-52362-x).

title: Representative certified nanoplastic reference materials
open: Can a family of certified nanoplastic reference materials be produced that faithfully represents real environmental nanoplastics rather than idealized laboratory analogues — spanning weathered polymers, irregular shapes, additive mixtures, size ranges, and environmental matrices, with independently certified properties?
status: Reference materials already exist; work published online in 2025 (Pegoraro et al., 2026; online 2025, *Nanoplastic reference materials for biological and methodological assessment*, DOI:10.1186/s43591-025-00157-2) introduced laser-generated model particles and discussed NPPP-1. However, representative coverage across realistic nanoplastic diversity and cross-method certification remain incomplete.
solved_when: A set of reference materials exists that covers weathered polymers, irregular particle shapes, additive mixtures, the relevant size ranges and environmental matrices, and whose properties are certified by independent, traceable, cross-method characterization.
why: Such references are the precondition for reproducible recovery estimates, meaningful comparison of analytical methods, and reliable dose–response experiments in nanoplastic toxicology.
key_works: Pegoraro et al. (2026; online 2025), *Nanoplastic reference materials for biological and methodological assessment*, [DOI:10.1186/s43591-025-00157-2](https://doi.org/10.1186/s43591-025-00157-2).

title: Closing organofluorine mass balances in complex products
open: Can we account for all the fluorine in a complex real-world sample — quantitatively reconciling total fluorine with its extractable, inorganic, polymeric, and individually identified organofluorine fractions within validated uncertainties? The challenge is to achieve closure of the fluorine mass balance for realistic commercial products and environmental samples, not just simple matrices.
status: Targeted PFAS assays leave substantial unidentified organofluorine fractions. A 2018 cosmetics study (Schultes et al., 2018, *Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances and fluorine mass balance in cosmetic products from the Swedish market: implications for environmental emissions and human exposure*, DOI:10.1039/C8EM00368H) demonstrated significant mass-balance gaps in real products. General analytical closure across complex products and environmental samples remains open.
solved_when: A validated analytical workflow demonstrates fluorine mass-balance closure on realistic products and environmental samples, with total, extractable, inorganic, polymeric, and target-identified fluorine measurements agreeing within stated, validated uncertainties.
why: Without closure, targeted PFAS testing can miss major fluorinated reservoirs — entire classes of fluorinated content that evade standard assays and thus go unregulated and untracked in exposure and emissions assessments.
key_works: Schultes et al. (2018), *Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances and fluorine mass balance in cosmetic products from the Swedish market: implications for environmental emissions and human exposure*, [DOI:10.1039/C8EM00368H](https://doi.org/10.1039/C8EM00368H).

title: Tire antiozonants without hazardous transformation products
open: Can a tire antiozonant be found that protects rubber as effectively as 6PPD while producing neither hazardous transformation products (such as 6PPD-quinone) nor comparably hazardous substitutes and emissions?
status: 6PPD-quinone toxicity was identified in 2020–2021 (Tian et al. (2021), *A ubiquitous tire rubber-derived chemical induces acute mortality in coho salmon*, [DOI:10.1126/science.abd6951](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.abd6951)); California DTSC's alternatives-analysis process for *Motor Vehicle Tires Containing 6PPD* documents continuing evaluation rather than an established universal substitute.
solved_when: A replacement chemistry is demonstrated that preserves tire durability and road safety at parity with 6PPD and whose parent compound, transformation products, and emissions are shown not to be comparably hazardous.
why: It would reduce aquatic harm — such as the acute mortality 6PPD-quinone causes in coho salmon — without sacrificing tire performance.
key_works: Tian et al. (2021), *A ubiquitous tire rubber-derived chemical induces acute mortality in coho salmon*, [DOI:10.1126/science.abd6951](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.abd6951); California DTSC, [*Motor Vehicle Tires Containing 6PPD*](https://dtsc.ca.gov/scp/motor_vehicle_tires_containing_6ppd/).

title: Predicting oil-paint and acrylic-ground interfacial failure
open: When and why does an oil paint film fail at its acrylic ground — cracking, protruding, or delaminating — given its chemistry and environmental history? A successful answer would take measurable chemical and environmental inputs and predict the onset and mode of interfacial failure.
status: Many of the individual degradation reactions are known. Interface-resolved analyses in 2025 (Gnemmi et al., *Early degradation mechanisms at the interface between acrylic grounds and oil paint films*, [DOI:10.1038/s40494-025-01861-1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s40494-025-01861-1)) linked early damage to chemical changes at the interface, but a generally predictive lifetime model remains open.
solved_when: A generally predictive lifetime model exists that, from measured pigment–binder–ground chemistry and environmental history, forecasts whether and when cracking, protrusions, or delamination develop.
why: It would let conservators intervene preventively before irreversible visible damage occurs, rather than reacting after cracking or flaking appears.
key_works: Gnemmi et al. (2025), *Early degradation mechanisms at the interface between acrylic grounds and oil paint films*, [DOI:10.1038/s40494-025-01861-1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s40494-025-01861-1).

title: Optimal Lieb–Oxford constant
open: What is the exact value of the smallest universal constant in the Lieb–Oxford inequality, which bounds the indirect Coulomb energy of a quantum system by a constant times the integral of the electron density to the four-thirds power? The question separates into distinct sharp constants for the unrestricted inequality, the exchange-only case, and physically restricted classes of states.
status: The problem has been open since the 1981 inequality. Lewin, Lieb and Seiringer (2022) proved an upper bound of approximately 1.58, while the best known lower bound exceeds 1.44, leaving the sharp value undetermined.
solved_when: The sharp constant is determined exactly — or, at minimum, the gap between the known bounds is closed: the upper bound of approximately 1.58 from Lewin, Lieb and Seiringer (2022) is matched with the known lower bound exceeding 1.44.
why: A sharper exact constraint would directly improve the mathematical foundation of exchange–correlation approximations in density-functional theory.
key_works: M. Lewin, E. H. Lieb and R. Seiringer (2022), *Improved Lieb–Oxford bound on the indirect and exchange energies*, [arXiv:2203.12473](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.12473), DOI: 10.1007/s11005-022-01584-5.

title: Practical density functional satisfying the full flat-plane condition
open: Can a single practical density functional be constructed that satisfies the full flat-plane condition — piecewise linearity in electron number together with constancy under fractional spin — while still delivering accurate energies, densities, and forces across bond breaking, without case-specific corrections or artificial symmetry breaking?
status: The fractional-charge and fractional-spin failures of density functional theory were unified in 2008–2009 (Cohen, Mori-Sánchez and Yang, 2008, DOI:10.1126/science.1158722). Fractional-spin corrections were demonstrated on successful molecular examples in 2018 (Su, Li and Yang, 2018), but a broadly transferable solution remains open.
solved_when: One affordable, broadly transferable functional satisfies both fractional-charge piecewise linearity and fractional-spin constancy, and demonstrably gives reliable energies, densities, and forces across bond-breaking situations.
why: A single such approximation would describe charge localization and static correlation consistently, removing the need for separate fixes for each failure mode.
key_works: A. J. Cohen, P. Mori-Sánchez and W. Yang (2008), *Insights into current limitations of density functional theory*, [DOI:10.1126/science.1158722](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1158722); N. Q. Su, C. Li and W. Yang (2018), *Describing strong correlation with fractional-spin correction in density functional theory*, [article](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6166809/).

title: Predictive exchange–correlation steps in charge separation
open: Can the spatial steps and derivative discontinuities in the exchange–correlation potential that enforce correct electron allocation between weakly coupled fragments during dissociation and charge transfer be predicted — in position and height — from the system itself?
status: The problem has been recognized for decades. Analytical work in 2025 (N. E. Rahat and E. Kraisler, *Plateaus in the Potentials of Density-Functional Theory: Analytical Derivation and Useful Approximations*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jctc.4c01771](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.4c01771)) derived the plateaus and investigated approximations, building on foundational understanding of the derivative discontinuity (P. Mori-Sánchez and A. J. Cohen, 2014, [article](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24920317/)); an inexpensive general reproduction remains unresolved.
solved_when: An inexpensive, general method reproduces the plateau structure and derivative discontinuities, correctly assigning fractional charge between fragments in dissociation and charge-transfer scenarios, without system-specific tuning.
why: Incorrect fractional charge corrupts redox energetics and charge-transfer mechanisms, undermining density-functional descriptions of these processes.
key_works: N. E. Rahat and E. Kraisler (2025), *Plateaus in the Potentials of Density-Functional Theory: Analytical Derivation and Useful Approximations*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jctc.4c01771](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.4c01771); P. Mori-Sánchez and A. J. Cohen (2014), *The derivative discontinuity of the exchange-correlation functional*, [article](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24920317/).

title: Chemically useful tractable classes of the fermion sign problem
open: Are there substantial, explicitly defined families of molecular Hamiltonians for which unbiased quantum Monte Carlo avoids exponential sign degradation — and where such families do not exist, can hardness be proved within them? In other words, characterize the boundary between chemically useful tractable classes and provably hard ones.
status: Troyer and Wiese established generic sign-problem NP-hardness in 2005 (*Computational Complexity and Fundamental Limitations to Fermionic Quantum Monte Carlo Simulations*, DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.94.170201). That result leaves the practical tractability boundary for structured molecular families incompletely characterized.
solved_when: A characterization is given of explicitly defined molecular Hamiltonian families either admitting unbiased quantum Monte Carlo free of exponential sign degradation, or proven hard within those families, thereby resolving the practical tractability boundary for structured molecular systems.
why: A classification would tell chemists precisely when unbiased correlation calculations can scale to interesting molecules, and when approximate or alternative methods are unavoidable.
key_works: M. Troyer and U.-J. Wiese (2005), *Computational Complexity and Fundamental Limitations to Fermionic Quantum Monte Carlo Simulations*, [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.94.170201](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.94.170201).

title: Robust transition-metal spin-state energetics
open: Can we predict spin-state free energies and equilibrium spin populations for transition-metal complexes reliably across oxidation states, temperatures, and solvents — with uncertainties that are actually calibrated rather than merely small?
status: The problem is decades old. The 2024 SSE17 comparison (M. Radoń et al., *Performance of quantum chemistry methods for a benchmark set of spin-state energetics derived from experimental data of 17 transition metal complexes (SSE17)*, [DOI:10.1039/D4SC05471G](https://doi.org/10.1039/D4SC05471G)) found CCSD(T) best among the methods tested, with a mean absolute electronic-energy error of 1.5 kcal/mol.
solved_when: A method reproduces spin-state free energies (not just electronic energies) across oxidation states, temperatures, and solvents, with calibrated uncertainties; for calibration, beating CCSD(T)'s SSE17 benchmark performance (mean absolute electronic-energy error of 1.5 kcal/mol) on experimentally derived data would be the natural target.
why: Spin populations govern magnetic properties and determine reaction pathways, so trustworthy predictions of them would make computational screening of transition-metal chemistry meaningful.
key_works: M. Radoń et al. (2024), *Performance of quantum chemistry methods for a benchmark set of spin-state energetics derived from experimental data of 17 transition metal complexes (SSE17)*, [DOI:10.1039/D4SC05471G](https://doi.org/10.1039/D4SC05471G).

title: Certified control of fixed-node bias
open: Can we bound the fixed-node energy error in diffusion Monte Carlo calculations of complex molecules, or design a procedure that demonstrably drives that error down to any prescribed tolerance? In formal terms, this asks for either computable a posteriori bounds on the nodal bias or a convergent sequence of trial nodes with certified error control.
status: Fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo has been powerful for decades, but nodal bias remains difficult to certify. Neural trial wavefunctions improved molecular calculations in 2023 (Ren, Fu, Wu and Chen, *Towards the ground state of molecules via diffusion Monte Carlo on neural networks*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-023-37609-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-37609-3); [arXiv:2204.13903](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.13903)), yet small sampling errors do not certify small nodal errors.
solved_when: A method exists that, for complex molecules, yields usable (quantitative) bounds on the fixed-node energy error, or a demonstrably convergent procedure that reduces the nodal error to any prescribed tolerance specified in advance.
why: Certification would make numerical predictions from fixed-node Monte Carlo quantitatively trustworthy; small statistical sampling errors currently give no guarantee that the nodal error is small.
key_works: W. Ren, W. Fu, X. Wu and J. Chen (2023), *Towards the ground state of molecules via diffusion Monte Carlo on neural networks*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-023-37609-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-37609-3); [arXiv:2204.13903](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.13903).

title: Affordable coupled electron–nuclear quantum dynamics
open: Can we make full electron–nuclear quantum dynamics — where both electrons and nuclei evolve quantum mechanically in real time — affordable enough to simulate chemically useful reactions, while keeping spatial discretization, pseudopotential, and readout errors under control?
status: A 2025 proposal (F. H. da Jornada et al., *A comprehensive framework to simulate real-time chemical dynamics on a fault-tolerant quantum computer*, [arXiv:2504.06348](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.06348), preprint) estimated 808 logical qubits and approximately \(10^{11}\) Toffoli gates per femtosecond for an ammonia–boron-trifluoride example; affordable implementation remains a substantial gap.
solved_when: A fault-tolerant quantum simulation of coupled electron–nuclear real-time dynamics is achieved at a resource cost materially below the current estimate of 808 logical qubits and roughly \(10^{11}\) Toffoli gates per femtosecond (benchmarked on the ammonia–boron-trifluoride example), with errors from spatial discretization, pseudopotentials, and observable readout controlled to chemically useful accuracy.
why: It would unlock first-principles simulation of reactions where electronic transitions and nuclear tunneling are inseparable, regimes inaccessible to methods that treat nuclei classically.
key_works: F. H. da Jornada et al. (2025), *A comprehensive framework to simulate real-time chemical dynamics on a fault-tolerant quantum computer*, [arXiv:2504.06348](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.06348), preprint.

title: Entanglement-assisted selection of bimolecular products
open: Can entanglement between reactant molecules be used in the laboratory as a control knob that selects which products a bimolecular reaction yields? Formally: demonstrate experimentally that deliberately entangled reactant states alter product-state branching beyond what is achievable by ordinary reactant-state preparation.
status: A 2025 calculation (Devoucher, Tscherbul, and Brumer, *Leveraging Reactant Entanglement in the Coherent Control of Ultracold Bimolecular Chemical Reactions*, DOI:10.1103/7c2n-xkpg; arXiv:2505.10684) predicted complete control of product rotational parity for an ultracold KRb + KRb example; experimental implementation and generalization to other reactions remain open.
solved_when: An experiment realizes entanglement-assisted product-state selection in a bimolecular reaction — e.g., implementing the predicted complete control of product rotational parity for ultracold KRb + KRb — and cleanly separates the entanglement contribution from that of classical reactant-state preparation.
why: Success would establish entanglement as an independent resource for chemical selectivity, adding a genuinely quantum handle to the control of reaction outcomes.
key_works: A. Devolder, T. Tscherbul and P. Brumer (2025), *Leveraging Reactant Entanglement in the Coherent Control of Ultracold Bimolecular Chemical Reactions*, [DOI:10.1103/7c2n-xkpg](https://doi.org/10.1103/7c2n-xkpg); [arXiv:2505.10684](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10684).

title: Isotope shifts of water’s liquid–liquid transition
open: How much does swapping hydrogen for deuterium shift water’s hypothesized liquid–liquid transition and its critical point? An answer requires measuring the H₂O–D₂O differences in liquid–liquid coexistence and critical parameters experimentally, together with theoretical predictions whose electronic and nuclear quantum errors are controlled.
status: Path-integral calculations, including a 2026 equation-of-state study (A. Eltareb et al. (2026), *Nuclear Quantum Effects on the Equation of State of Water: Insights from the Potential Energy Landscape Formalism*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jctc.5c02151](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.5c02151)), quantify the shifts within specific models, but a model-independent experimental phase diagram for both isotopes is still missing.
solved_when: The liquid–liquid coexistence regions and critical parameters are experimentally mapped for both H₂O and D₂O in a model-independent way, and the isotope shifts between them are reproduced by calculations with quantified electronic-structure and nuclear-quantum-error control.
why: Isotope substitution is a clean dial for nuclear quantum effects, so comparing H₂O and D₂O separates quantum contributions from classical hydrogen-bond network mechanisms in water’s anomalies.
key_works: A. Eltareb et al. (2026), *Nuclear Quantum Effects on the Equation of State of Water: Insights from the Potential Energy Landscape Formalism*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jctc.5c02151](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.5c02151).

title: Convention-consistent single-ion hydration energetics
open: Can theory and experiment be brought to agree on the hydration free energy of a single ion once both sides adopt the same surface-potential and electrochemical conventions? A satisfactory answer would quantify the electronic, finite-size, and interfacial error contributions on each side of the comparison.
status: The issue has been debated for decades. Quantum simulations now provide operationally defined scales, as in the 2017 study of Duignan, Baer, Schenter, and Mundy (*Real single ion solvation free energies with quantum mechanical simulation*, [DOI:10.1039/C7SC02138K](https://doi.org/10.1039/C7SC02138K)), but broad transferable accuracy remains incomplete, and a convention-free absolute single-ion number is not a physically appropriate target.
solved_when: Calculated and experimentally inferred single-ion hydration free energies agree within stated error budgets under shared conventions, with the electronic, finite-size, and interfacial errors each quantified.
why: Single-ion energetics govern acidity, solubility, and electrochemical interfaces, so a convention-consistent scale makes these quantities reliably comparable across methods and experiments.
key_works: T. T. Duignan, M. D. Baer, G. K. Schenter and C. J. Mundy (2017), *Real single ion solvation free energies with quantum mechanical simulation*, [DOI:10.1039/C7SC02138K](https://doi.org/10.1039/C7SC02138K).

title: Surface dependence of anomalous electrolyte underscreening
open: When a concentrated electrolyte shows an anomalously long force-decay length, is this a property of bulk screening, of ion clustering, or of the specific surface involved — and can a single predictive framework capture how the effect depends on salt concentration and substrate across different measurement methods?
status: Positive and null observations of anomalous underscreening coexist. A 2025 simulation by D. Ribar, C. E. Woodward and J. Forsman (*Solvent-induced ion clusters generate long-ranged double-layer forces at high ionic strengths*, [DOI:10.1039/D5SM00027K](https://doi.org/10.1039/D5SM00027K)) connected long-ranged forces to solvent-induced clusters but did not reproduce the full concentration dependence.
solved_when: A theory (validated by experiment and/or simulation) predicts the concentration and substrate dependence of long force-decay lengths in concentrated electrolytes consistently across measurement methods, and identifies the mechanism (bulk screening, clustering, or surface-specific effects) responsible.
why: Screening models underpin predictions of colloidal stability and of how ions organize at interfaces, so settling the mechanism directly affects what these models can reliably forecast.
key_works: D. Ribar, C. E. Woodward and J. Forsman (2025), *Solvent-induced ion clusters generate long-ranged double-layer forces at high ionic strengths*, [DOI:10.1039/D5SM00027K](https://doi.org/10.1039/D5SM00027K).

title: Complete structure searches for flexible molecular crystals
open: Can we generate the full set of experimentally relevant low-free-energy crystal packings for flexible molecules, salts, and coordination compounds — and know when the search is complete? Formally, the goal is structure-generation methods whose outputs provably, or with meaningful diagnostics, cover the low-free-energy landscape rather than merely sampling it.
status: The seventh blind test, reported in 2024, showed stronger performance for simple targets than for complex systems, and two groups first blindly predicted disorder.
solved_when: All experimentally relevant low-free-energy packings of flexible molecules, salts, and coordination compounds are generated, together with meaningful search-completeness diagnostics.
why: Energy ranking, however accurate, cannot recover a relevant structure that was never generated; without complete generation, downstream ranking silently misses real polymorphs.
key_works: L. M. Hunnisett et al. (2024), *The seventh blind test of crystal structure prediction: structure generation methods*, [DOI:10.1107/S2052520624007492](https://doi.org/10.1107/S2052520624007492).

title: Predicting cocrystal stoichiometry and competing phases
open: Can we predict, from the molecular components alone, which stoichiometries a multicomponent crystal will adopt and whether the true outcome is a cocrystal at all rather than separate crystals, a salt, a solvate, or a disordered phase? Formally, this asks for a joint predictor of composition and structure whose output can be checked against composition-dependent phase diagrams.
status: The 2024 seventh blind test of crystal structure prediction (L. M. Hunnisett et al. (2024), *The seventh blind test of crystal structure prediction: structure generation methods*, [DOI:10.1107/S2052520624007492](https://doi.org/10.1107/S2052520624007492)) explored stoichiometry prediction and found promising approaches; a generally reliable joint composition-and-structure predictor remains open.
solved_when: A generally reliable method exists that predicts cocrystal stoichiometries and discriminates among competing phases (separate crystals, salts, solvates, disordered phases), validated against composition-dependent phase diagrams across the blind-test-style targets.
why: Stoichiometry determines material properties and synthetic accessibility, so a reliable predictor would tell chemists not just how a multicomponent crystal packs but whether it forms usefully at all.
key_works: L. M. Hunnisett et al. (2024), *The seventh blind test of crystal structure prediction: structure generation methods*, [DOI:10.1107/S2052520624007492](https://doi.org/10.1107/S2052520624007492).

title: Reliable polymorph stability ranking at ambient conditions
open: Can we compute the relative free energies of competing molecular-crystal polymorphs accurately enough that the ranking at ambient conditions is reliable — that is, with computational errors smaller than the free-energy gaps separating the forms, fully accounting for thermal, quantum, and disorder effects?
status: In the seventh blind test of crystal structure prediction (2024), dispersion-corrected periodic DFT often agreed with experiment on stability rankings, but thermal corrections helped only some targets, and the calculations remained costly (L. M. Hunnisett et al. (2024), *The seventh blind test of crystal structure prediction: structure ranking methods*, [DOI:10.1107/S2052520624008679](https://doi.org/10.1107/S2052520624008679)).
solved_when: A method ranks closely competing polymorph free energies at ambient conditions with errors below their free-energy separations, including thermal, quantum, and disorder effects.
why: The stability ordering dictates which solid form a material converts to, so it governs shelf-life and formulation risks for molecular solids.
key_works: L. M. Hunnisett et al. (2024), *The seventh blind test of crystal structure prediction: structure ranking methods*, [DOI:10.1107/S2052520624008679](https://doi.org/10.1107/S2052520624008679).

title: Predicted missing stable polymorph of blind-test target XXXII
open: Does target XXXII from the seventh crystal structure prediction blind test possess an experimentally accessible polymorph more stable than any form observed so far — and if not, why does the prediction fail?
status: Several 2024 blind-test methods placed the observed forms over 4 kJ/mol above the predicted minima [L. M. Hunnisett et al. (2024), *The seventh blind test of crystal structure prediction: structure ranking methods*, DOI:10.1107/S2052520624008679], and a 2025 study still identified the missing global minimum [J. van de Streek et al. (2025), *A Conceptual Framework for the Crystallizability of Organic Compounds*, DOI:10.1021/jacs.5c08933].
solved_when: Either the predicted lower-free-energy polymorph is produced and experimentally characterized, or a rigorous account is given of why its predicted stability (lying more than 4 kJ/mol below observed forms) or its crystallization accessibility fails.
why: It is a concrete test case for whether computational crystal structure prediction can genuinely guide the discovery of hidden solid forms, or whether predicted global minima can be persistively unreachable artifacts.
key_works: L. M. Hunnisett et al. (2024), *The seventh blind test of crystal structure prediction: structure ranking methods*, [DOI:10.1107/S2052520624008679](https://doi.org/10.1107/S2052520624008679); J. van de Streek et al. (2025), *A Conceptual Framework for the Crystallizability of Organic Compounds*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.5c08933](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c08933).

title: Affordable anharmonic lattice free energies
open: Can we compute converged anharmonic free-energy differences for large libraries of flexible and disordered molecular polymorphs — including controlled finite-size errors — at a cost practical for routine screening? Formally, this asks for a method whose free-energy differences are converged with respect to anharmonic and finite-size effects while scaling to library-sized sets of molecular crystals.
status: Normalizing-flow calculations gave accurate free energies for two modeled ice polymorphs in 2025 (E. Olehnovics et al., *Accurate Lattice Free Energies of Packing Polymorphs from Probabilistic Generative Models*, DOI:10.1021/acs.jctc.4c01612). Diverse molecular crystals remain a broader transfer and scaling challenge.
solved_when: A method delivers converged anharmonic free-energy differences, with finite-size errors accounted for, for large libraries of flexible and disordered molecular polymorphs at practical computational cost.
why: Anharmonic entropy can reverse polymorph stability rankings, so affordable converged free energies determine whether crystal-structure prediction and polymorph screening can be trusted for real molecular solids.
key_works: E. Olehnovics et al. (2025), *Accurate Lattice Free Energies of Packing Polymorphs from Probabilistic Generative Models*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jctc.4c01612](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.4c01612).

title: Carrier of the 5780 Å diffuse interstellar band
open: What molecule, ion, or other carrier produces the diffuse interstellar absorption band at 5780 Å? An answer requires laboratory spectra that match the astronomical wavelength, band profile, and any companion transitions, together with a plausible interstellar abundance.
status: The band has remained unidentified since Heger's 1922 report. A 2025 quantum-chemical study by H. Seuret et al. (Vetting molecular candidates posited for the first diffuse interstellar bands (5780 and 5797 Å): a quantum chemical study, DOI:10.1039/D4CP04023F) rejected several proposed molecular families on the grounds of incompatible spectra.
solved_when: A specific carrier is identified whose laboratory spectrum reproduces the observed 5780 Å band position and profile (and companion transitions), with an abundance consistent with interstellar conditions.
why: Identification would convert a widespread absorption feature into a chemical diagnostic for the interstellar medium, constraining the composition and chemistry of diffuse clouds.
key_works: H. Seuret et al. (2025), *Vetting molecular candidates posited for the first diffuse interstellar bands (5780 and 5797 Å): a quantum chemical study*, [DOI:10.1039/D4CP04023F](https://doi.org/10.1039/D4CP04023F).

title: Carrier of the 5797 Å diffuse interstellar band
open: Which molecule in the interstellar medium absorbs light at 5797 Å to produce this diffuse interstellar band? A successful carrier assignment must reproduce the band's spectrum and its environmental dependence on its own, without leaning on the assignment of the neighboring 5780 Å band.
status: The problem has been open since 1922. Correlated band families and candidate calculations constrain the possibilities, but no confirmed molecular assignment exists; recent work includes H. Seuret et al. (2025), *Vetting molecular candidates posited for the first diffuse interstellar bands (5780 and 5797 Å): a quantum chemical study*, [DOI:10.1039/D4CP04023F](https://doi.org/10.1039/D4CP04023F).
solved_when: A specific molecule is identified whose calculated spectrum matches the observed 5797 Å band profile and whose behavior reproduces the band's observed environmental dependence, established independently of any assignment of the 5780 Å band.
why: The carrier would be a chemically informative component of interstellar matter, revealing what molecules actually exist and survive in the diffuse interstellar medium.
key_works: H. Seuret et al. (2025), *Vetting molecular candidates posited for the first diffuse interstellar bands (5780 and 5797 Å): a quantum chemical study*, [DOI:10.1039/D4CP04023F](https://doi.org/10.1039/D4CP04023F).

title: Missing interstellar oxygen reservoir
open: Where is the oxygen that observations of translucent and dense interstellar clouds cannot account for in gas, silicates, or conventional ices? Identify the carrier of this hidden reservoir, quantify it, and close the elemental oxygen abundance budget using diagnostic spectra.
status: A longstanding depletion discrepancy persists, with a significant fraction of oxygen unaccounted for. A 2025 analysis by T. Onaka, I. Sakon, T. Shimonishi and M. Honda (2025), *Searching for missing interstellar oxygen in the far-infrared* ([arXiv:2509.01846](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.01846)), identifies far-infrared signatures of large icy grains as a discriminating observation.
solved_when: The missing oxygen in translucent and dense clouds is located and its abundance quantified, such that the observed gas, silicate, ice, and newly identified reservoirs together close the total oxygen budget, with the identification confirmed through diagnostic spectra.
why: How oxygen partitions among gas, dust, and ice phases directly constrains the composition of planet-forming material and the delivery of water to planets.
key_works: T. Onaka, I. Sakon, T. Shimonishi and M. Honda (2025), *Searching for missing interstellar oxygen in the far-infrared*, [arXiv:2509.01846](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.01846).

title: Cold-cloud formation or survival of pyrene
open: Can pyrene in the cold cloud TMC-1 be built in situ at low temperature, or must it instead survive transport from warmer regions — and which scenario reproduces the observed abundances and nitrile-isomer ratios under physically constrained kinetics?
status: Cyanopyrene detections in 2024–2025 established four-ring aromatic chemistry in a cold cloud (G. Wenzel et al. 2024, *Detection of interstellar 1-cyanopyrene: A four-ring polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon*, [DOI:10.1126/science.adq6391](https://doi.org/10.1126/science/adq6391); G. Wenzel et al. 2025, *Detections of interstellar aromatic nitriles 2-cyanopyrene and 4-cyanopyrene in TMC-1*, [DOI:10.1038/s41550-024-02410-9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41550-024-02410-9)). The parent aromatic inventory's origin remains unresolved.
solved_when: A formation or survival pathway is identified that reproduces the observed pyrene (via cyanopyrene) abundances and nitrile-isomer ratios in TMC-1 using a kinetics scheme whose rates and pathways are physically constrained.
why: It tests how large carbon molecules arise before star formation, determining whether complex aromatic chemistry is a local product of cold clouds or an inheritance from warmer environments.
key_works: G. Wenzel et al. (2024), *Detection of interstellar 1-cyanopyrene: A four-ring polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon*, [DOI:10.1126/science.adq6391](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adq6391); G. Wenzel et al. (2025), *Detections of interstellar aromatic nitriles 2-cyanopyrene and 4-cyanopyrene in TMC-1*, [DOI:10.1038/s41550-024-02410-9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41550-024-02410-9).

title: Interstellar enantiomeric excess
open: Can we measure the handedness of a chiral molecule in interstellar space — a nonzero enantiomeric excess, or a meaningful upper bound on it — using observations sensitive to handedness with polarization errors under control?
status: Propylene oxide was detected in 2016 by B. A. McGuire et al. (*Discovery of the interstellar chiral molecule propylene oxide (CH3CHCH2O)*, [arXiv:1606.07483](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.07483)), establishing the molecule's identity but not measuring its handedness. Meteorite measurements concern different samples and histories and so do not address the interstellar case.
solved_when: A handedness-sensitive observation of an interstellar chiral molecule, with controlled polarization systematics, yields either a detected nonzero enantiomeric excess or a quantitative upper bound on it.
why: It would constrain how much astronomical environments contribute to the biological handedness (homochirality) seen on Earth.
key_works: B. A. McGuire et al. (2016), *Discovery of the interstellar chiral molecule propylene oxide (CH3CHCH2O)*, [arXiv:1606.07483](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.07483).

title: Synthesis and identification of element 119
open: Can element 119 be synthesized and its identity firmly established? The goal is to produce nuclei with atomic number 119 and demonstrate their existence through reproducible decay chains or direct mass evidence.
status: Element 119 remains a search target according to the 2026 experimental review by J. M. Gates and J. L. Pore, *The Quest for Superheavy Nuclei: An Experimental Perspective* ([DOI:10.1146/annurev-nucl-100324-103404](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-nucl-100324-103404)). A 2022 quasielastic barrier distribution measurement by M. Tanaka et al. ([DOI:10.7566/JPSJ.91.084201](https://doi.org/10.7566/JPSJ.91.084201)) constrained the optimal reaction energies for the ⁵¹V + ²⁴⁸Cm fusion route but did not achieve synthesis.
solved_when: Nuclei with atomic number 119 have been produced and their identity established through reproducible decay or mass evidence.
why: It would open the eighth period of the periodic table and provide a direct test of nuclear stability predictions and relativistic effects on periodicity in superheavy elements.
key_works: M. Tanaka et al. (2022), *Probing Optimal Reaction Energy for Synthesis of Element 119 from 51V+248Cm Reaction with Quasielastic Barrier Distribution Measurement*, [DOI:10.7566/JPSJ.91.084201](https://doi.org/10.7566/JPSJ.91.084201); J. M. Gates and J. L. Pore (2026), *The Quest for Superheavy Nuclei: An Experimental Perspective*, [DOI:10.1146/annurev-nucl-100324-103404](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-nucl-100324-103404).

title: Synthesis and identification of element 120
open: Can element 120 be synthesized in the laboratory and its identity established beyond doubt? The goal is to produce element 120 and identify it through decay assignments and reaction evidence strong enough to permit independent confirmation.
status: Searches for element 120 remained underway as of the 2026 review by Gates and Pore. Production of livermorium (Z=116) using a ⁵⁰Ti beam in 2024 (Gates et al.) demonstrated the precursor technology required for heavier-element synthesis.
solved_when: Element 120 has been produced and its decay chains and formation reaction are characterized to a standard sufficient for independent confirmation by other laboratories.
why: A confirmed discovery would test shell-stabilization predictions near the superheavy island of stability and extend experimentally known periodicity of the elements.
key_works: J. M. Gates et al. (2024), *Toward the Discovery of New Elements: Production of Livermorium (Z=116) with 50Ti*, [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.133.172502](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.133.172502); J. M. Gates and J. L. Pore (2026), *The Quest for Superheavy Nuclei: An Experimental Perspective*, [DOI:10.1146/annurev-nucl-100324-103404](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-nucl-100324-103404).

title: Experimental chemical properties of oganesson
open: Can any chemical or response property of oganesson — such as adsorption, polarizability, or molecular binding — be measured experimentally, and does the result confirm the predicted departures from lighter noble gases?
status: Individual nuclei exist, but chemical behavior remains computationally inferred. A 2020 calculation by O. R. Smits et al. (*Oganesson: A Noble Gas Element That Is Neither Noble Nor a Gas*, [DOI:10.1002/anie.202011976](https://doi.org/10.1002/anie.202011976)) predicted major departures from lighter noble gases; atom scarcity and short lifetimes obstruct experiments.
solved_when: A direct experimental measurement of an oganesson chemical or response property (e.g., adsorption, polarizability, or molecular binding) is obtained and compared against relativistic predictions.
why: Oganesson is an extreme test of the basis of periodic trends; a measurement would replace computationally inferred behavior with experimental fact.
key_works: O. R. Smits et al. (2020), *Oganesson: A Noble Gas Element That Is Neither Noble Nor a Gas*, [DOI:10.1002/anie.202011976](https://doi.org/10.1002/anie.202011976).

title: Defect-controlled thorium isomer quenching
open: Can we deliberately engineer defects in a thorium-isomer host that switch the nuclear state on demand — enabling readout or reset — without degrading the coherence and frequency stability needed during interrogation? Formally, the goal is a materials design in which defect-mediated quenching is controllable and the clock's frequency stability survives the measurement cycle.
status: Photoinduced quenching of the 229Th isomer in a solid-state host was demonstrated in 2025, and defect-mediated internal conversion explains the observations (J. E. S. Terhune et al. (2025), *Photoinduced quenching of the 229Th isomer in a solid-state host*, [DOI:10.1103/glzr-thyw](https://doi.org/10.1103/glzr-thyw)). However, reproducible materials design with quantified clock tradeoffs remains open.
solved_when: A reproducible defect-engineering protocol exists that demonstrates efficient, switchable quenching of the 229Th isomer while quantifying the tradeoff between reset/readout speed and clock coherence and frequency stability.
why: A controlled reset mechanism would shorten measurement cycles for the thorium nuclear clock and improve detection of the isomer state.
key_works: J. E. S. Terhune et al. (2025), *Photoinduced quenching of the 229Th isomer in a solid-state host*, [DOI:10.1103/glzr-thyw](https://doi.org/10.1103/glzr-thyw).

title: Productive direct aqueous dinitrogen electroreduction
open: Can purified dinitrogen be converted directly to ammonia in water, at useful rates and selectivity, without any reactive-metal mediator — and reproducibly?
status: Pursued for decades, with contamination remaining the decisive obstacle. Schneider et al. (2025), *Reevaluating the Activity of ZIF-8 Based FeNCs for Electrochemical Ammonia Production*, found that reported Fe/Zn–N–C activity disappeared when nitrogen-oxide contamination was excluded.
solved_when: Net conversion of purified N₂ to ammonia in aqueous electrolysis is demonstrated at useful rates and selectivity, confirmed by isotope tracing and complete nitrogen balances, and independently replicated.
why: Success would simplify ammonia electrosynthesis by eliminating reactive-metal mediation, a longstanding complication in the field.
key_works: C. Schneider et al. (2025), *Reevaluating the Activity of ZIF-8 Based FeNCs for Electrochemical Ammonia Production*, [primary institutional record](https://www.materials.ox.ac.uk/publication/2352947/ora-hyrax).

title: Sacrificial-reagent-free molecular photofixation of nitrogen
open: Can molecular nitrogen reduction be coupled directly to water oxidation so that light, N₂, and water are the only net inputs and ammonia and oxygen are the only net products? In other words, can a molecular photofixation cycle be run without any sacrificial reagent?
status: Molecular nitrogen fixation has advanced since the early 2000s. Yamazaki et al. achieved visible-light-driven ammonia formation using water in 2025, though tertiary phosphines supplied the sacrificial reducing equivalents (Y. Yamazaki, Y. Endo and Y. Nishibayashi (2025), *Catalytic ammonia formation from dinitrogen, water, and visible light energy*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-59727-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59727-w)).
solved_when: A molecular system demonstrably produces NH₃ and O₂ as the net products from N₂, H₂O, and light input alone, with no sacrificial donor or reagent consumed.
why: It would establish a materially closed artificial photosynthetic ammonia cycle, replacing stoichiometric sacrificial reagents with water as the electron source.
key_works: Y. Yamazaki, Y. Endo and Y. Nishibayashi (2025), *Catalytic ammonia formation from dinitrogen, water, and visible light energy*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-59727-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59727-w).

title: Coke-resistant nonoxidative methane aromatization
open: Can methane be converted nonoxidatively to aromatics over a catalyst that resists coke buildup for sustained operation, without needing frequent regeneration cycles that degrade it? Formally, the goal is a catalyst design achieving stable methane-to-aromatics conversion where carbon-deposit nucleation and growth do not force periodic regenerative shutdowns.
status: A decades-old challenge. The state of the art is a 2024 Pt–Bi/Mo/ZSM-5 trimetallic synergistic catalyst (W. Bian et al., 2024, *Direct conversion of methane to aromatics and hydrogen via a heterogeneous trimetallic synergistic catalyst*, DOI:10.1038/s41467-024-47595-9), which reported 18.7% methane conversion and 69.4% benzene selectivity; catalyst lifetime and joint conversion–selectivity–stability performance remain the limiting factors.
solved_when: A catalyst sustains methane-to-aromatics conversion at or above the current benchmark of 18.7% methane conversion with 69.4% benzene selectivity (W. Bian et al., 2024, DOI:10.1038/s41467-024-47595-9) over an extended lifetime, without persistent coke formation and without frequent regeneration that damages the catalyst.
why: A solution co-produces aromatic feedstocks and hydrogen directly from methane in a single step, converting an abundant hydrocarbon into value-added chemicals and fuel.
key_works: W. Bian et al. (2024), *Direct conversion of methane to aromatics and hydrogen via a heterogeneous trimetallic synergistic catalyst*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-024-47595-9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-47595-9).

title: Multicarbon electrolysis of variable impure CO₂ feeds
open: Can a multicarbon CO₂ electrolyzer hold controlled, useful output when fed dilute, impure CO₂ streams whose oxygen, sulfur, and nitrogen contaminant levels vary over time, rather than requiring a purified feed?
status: Fang et al. tested dilute feeds and selected flue-gas impurities in 2026 (Thousand-hour salt precipitation-free CO₂-to-ethylene electrosynthesis at high current densities, DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-67719-z). Long-life operation under realistic mixed-impurity histories remains open.
solved_when: Continuous electrolysis on dilute CO₂ feeds with realistic time-varying mixed impurities (O, S, N species) sustains controlled multicarbon production, with poisoning, regeneration, and carbon balances quantitatively measured across the operating history.
why: Success would cut the upstream purification burden, letting electrolyzers run directly on impurity-laden dilute sources such as flue gas instead of costly cleaned CO₂.
key_works: M. Fang et al. (2026), *Thousand-hour salt precipitation-free CO2-to-ethylene electrosynthesis at high current densities*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-67719-z](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-67719-z).

title: Practical iridium-free acidic oxygen evolution
subfield: Water splitting, hydrogen production and fuel cells
open: Can a catalyst made entirely from earth-abundant elements drive oxygen evolution in acid at practically useful performance, and can its material losses be quantified rigorously enough to prove it survives?
status: The problem is long sought. A 2025 cobalt study (D. Simondson et al., *Decoupling the catalytic and degradation mechanisms of cobalt active sites during acidic water oxidation*, [DOI:10.1038/s41560-025-01812-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41560-025-01812-x)) separated catalysis, corrosion and regeneration, showing that self-reformation alone does not establish negligible material loss.
solved_when: An iridium-free catalyst is demonstrated in acidic oxygen evolution combining useful current density, low voltage, and long membrane-electrode-assembly lifetime, together with a complete dissolution balance accounting for material loss.
why: It would remove the critical-material (iridium scarcity) bottleneck currently limiting PEM hydrogen production scale-up.
key_works: D. Simondson et al. (2025), *Decoupling the catalytic and degradation mechanisms of cobalt active sites during acidic water oxidation*, [DOI:10.1038/s41560-025-01812-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41560-025-01812-x).

title: Material-based hydrogen storage meeting complete system targets
open: Can a material-based hydrogen storage system simultaneously meet the complete DOE ultimate targets of 6.5 wt% usable system capacity and 50 g/L system volumetric capacity? Formally, achieving this together with the delivery, refueling, cost, and lifetime requirements — not merely material-level uptake.
status: A decades-old target. Computational screening of nearly half a million MOFs produced high-performing materials in 2019 (Ahmed et al., DOI:10.1038/s41467-019-09365-w), but complete systems must also account for vessels, cooling, and unusable residual hydrogen (U.S. DOE technical targets table, accessed 2026-10-06).
solved_when: A complete storage system — including vessel, cooling, and unusable residual hydrogen — demonstrates 6.5 wt% and 50 g/L usable capacities simultaneously, while meeting the stated delivery, refueling, cost, and lifetime requirements.
why: It would enable compact hydrogen transport with competitive system mass and volume, moving storage from promising materials to deployable systems.
key_works: U.S. DOE, *DOE Technical Targets for Onboard Hydrogen Storage for Light-Duty Vehicles*, [official table, accessed 2026-10-06](https://www.energy.gov/cmei/fuels/doe-technical-targets-onboard-hydrogen-storage-light-duty-vehicles); A. Ahmed et al. (2019), *Exceptional hydrogen storage achieved by screening nearly half a million metal-organic frameworks*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-019-09365-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-09365-w).

title: Uniform maximum atomic excess charge
open: Is there a uniform ceiling on how many extra electrons an atom can hold? Formally, prove that a nucleus of charge \(Z\) can bind at most \(Z+C\) electrons, with \(C\) independent of \(Z\), for the full nonrelativistic many-electron Coulomb Hamiltonian.
status: The Hartree–Fock analogue is established, while the interacting Schrödinger problem remains open. A 2025 result gives the explicit bound \(N_c<1.1185Z+4Z^{1/3}\) for \(Z\ge4\), which still permits an excess increasing with nuclear charge.
solved_when: A proof (for the interacting Schrödinger problem) that the maximal binding charge satisfies \(N_c \le Z + C\) for some constant \(C\) independent of \(Z\).

title: All-weight extension of atomic ionization bounds
open: How many excess electrons can an atom of nuclear charge \(Z\) bind before the surplus charge falls off? Formally, prove that the maximal number of electrons satisfies \(N_c(Z) < b(s)Z + c(s)Z^{1/3}\) for every \(s \ge 1\), where \(b(s) = \max_{0 \le t \le 1}(1+t^{s-1})/(1+t^s)\) and \(c(s)\) is finite; the unresolved range is \(s > 3\), including quantitative control of \(c(s)\).
status: Hundertmark, Pattakos and Schulz proved the weighted estimate for \(1 < s \le 3\) and explicitly conjectured its extension in 2025 (Hundertmark, Pattakos and Schulz (2025), *On the Excess Charge Problem of Atoms*, Remark 2.3, [arXiv:2504.18487](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.18487)). The problem connects to weighted Hardy inequalities and uniform optimization bounds.
solved_when: The bound \(N_c(Z) < b(s)Z + c(s)Z^{1/3}\) is established for all \(s \ge 1\) (in particular \(s > 3\)), with a finite explicit constant \(c(s)\) whose quantitative dependence is controlled.
why: Since \(b(s) \to 1\) as \(s\) grows, proving the extension would substantially strengthen known ionization bounds for finite atoms, pushing the excess-charge constant toward its optimal value.
key_works: Hundertmark, Pattakos and Schulz (2025), *On the Excess Charge Problem of Atoms*, Remark 2.3, [arXiv:2504.18487](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.18487).

title: Uniform first-ionization-energy bound
open: Is the first ionization energy of a neutral atom bounded independently of the nuclear charge Z? Formally, prove that \(E_Z(Z-1)-E_Z(Z)\le C\) for a uniform constant C, in the full many-body Schrödinger model with the complete electron–electron interaction.
status: A longstanding component of the ionization conjecture. Solovej proved the Hartree–Fock version (J. P.
